_doc: Open sources of which trees make a forest's canopy, read by pipeline/tree_cards.py to choose a tile's dominant trees. plots: published plot inventories (abundance, basal area or importance value per species) with their location; a plot within tree_cards.PLOT_RADIUS_KM of a tile, at an elevation within PLOT_ELEV_M and in the tile's climate group, ranks the tile's trees. descriptions: open texts that name a place's characteristic or emergent trees, with the box (west, south, east, north) and elevation band they describe; each name is resolved to a WCVP species with the source of the resolution. Every entry carries its licence; only CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA sources are listed. Values were read by an agent from the source (figures read off a chart are marked so).

plots.citation: Vela-Apaza, C. I. & Gonzales-Ojeda, T. (2024). Flora arborea de los bosques de la planicie aluvial inundable en el Rio Los Amigos, Amazonia Peruana. Revista Biodiversidad Amazonica 3(1): e274
plots.licence: CC BY 4.0 (stated in the article PDF)
plots.where: four 1-ha plots (Bajio CM3, Bambu CM3, Cocha Lobo, Jacaratia) in the floodplain forest of the Los Amigos and Madre de Dios rivers, CICRA, Madre de Dios, Peru; three seasonally flooded, one on a terra firme terrace; trees >= 10 cm dbh, lianas excluded, 2097 stems, 317 species
plots.measure: importance value index (IVI = relative density + relative dominance + relative frequency), summed over the four plots
plots.measure_note: read off Figure 5 (stacked bars of the 20 most important species) to about +-1; abundance order (Figure 4) agrees: Iriartea deltoidea 284 stems, Pseudolmedia laevis 139, Euterpe precatoria 101, Socratea exorrhiza 94, Otoba parvifolia 83

descriptions.citation: Parque nacional del Manu, Wikipedia (Spanish), section on the lowland forest of the Manu river
descriptions.says: in the zone of the meandering Manu river the trees are gigantic, and some species emerge above their crowns: shihuahuaco (Dipteryx micrantha) and lupuna (Ceiba pentandra)

descriptions.citation: Corcovado National Park, Wikipedia (English), flora paragraph
descriptions.says: over 500 tree species, including purple heart, poponjoche, nargusta, banak, cow tree, espave and crabwood
